chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that his father and Sa'id ibn Abdullah said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (the first) (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

Ten groups of people put themselves and others through hardships: one with little knowledge who strives to teach people much; a patient man with much knowledge who lacks insight; one who pursues wealth that he cannot attain and does not deserve; one who strives hard but is not well-mannered; the well-mannered one who, despite his manners, lacks knowledge; a scholar who is not desirous of righteousness; one desirous of righteousness who is not a scholar; a scholar who loves the world; one kind to people who is stingy with what he possesses; and one seeking knowledge who argues with those who are more knowledgeable than him, and when they teach him, he does not accept it.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten types of people who put themselves and others through hardships according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (AS) delineates ten specific archetypes of spiritual and intellectual misalignment, highlighting how deficits in wisdom, timing, or intention corrupt otherwise neutral traits. This classification serves as a practical guide for self-assessment in Shia ethical tradition, warning against the perils of unearned authority, misplaced ambition, and the subtle corruption of knowledge by worldly desires.
